## Historical audit — S0339

**Scope:** Only chunk 1 of 2 is visible. All citations below refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/selection/bw_0045/1/trajectory.jsonl`. The reference and rendered images themselves are not visible in this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal: line 1, `model_request` | Reconstruct a 512 × 285 photograph as an editable SceneAct/Blender scene, matching viewpoint, framing, materials and occlusion. The student’s inventory interprets it as a dairy barn with cows, stall rails, beds, wall, door and worker; that interpretation is not independent image verification (line 3, H `model_response`). |
| Initial build: lines 3–10 | H supplied and executed a complete program with six cow calls despite comments estimating five, nine divider loops, architecture and a worker. Cow parts are separate ellipsoids and rods; rails use segmented rods and supports. Colors, metallic/roughness settings, surface marks, camera and lights were coded—not visually verified. Build and render completed; step 1 returned `ok: true` and was selected (line 9, `execution_result`, characters [0,38698); line 10). |
| Feedback and revision: lines 11–20 | The runner supplied the reference, render and comparison instructions. H **reported**, rather than independently established for this audit, small cow silhouettes, excessive foreground, low background and weak dark coverage (line 13). It changed camera, cow proportions and markings, rails, materials and lighting; step 2 built, rendered and was selected (lines 14, 16, 18–20; line 19 characters [0,38760)). The selected camera projected the door top at approximately (.401,.258), versus H’s estimated reference (.32,.02); its upward-aim trial moved it down to y=.279. These are point projections, not contour or visibility checks. |
| Further exploration: lines 21–28 | After another supplied render, H reported rear-facing rounded cows, shallow rail gaps and a misplaced door (line 23). It executed a third complete revision: a closer, more side-on camera, relocated door, longer bodies and heavier bent rails, with an old/chosen/trial projection routine (line 24). Build and render processes completed with return code 0 (lines 26, 28). The visible chunk contains no step-3 execution result, selection, final visual review or final submission. |

**Teacher input and autonomy.** No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update or student adoption is visible. The observed guidance is the task/runner’s generic comparison and projection procedure, not evidence of a teacher intervention. H did perform its own reported image comparisons and revisions; its sessions show no tool calls, while the external runner executed its programs (lines 2, 11–14, 21–24).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** This is operational success for the first two builds and completed third build/render processes, **not established reconstruction success**. No timeout or technical interruption is visible. Correct object count, actual part connections, poses, textures, illumination and final camera match remain unverified without the images. H’s reported discrepancies and its camera-versus-geometry diagnoses are hypotheses, not independent findings; step 3’s effect is unknown.

**Transferable lesson:** Render completion and landmark projections test execution and selected points, not visual completeness or correct connections. **Task-specific observation:** the student repeatedly revised cow silhouettes, divider gaps and barn framing, but the unseen final image prevents judging whether those changes helped.
